methodology: Two automated passes with a local qwen3:8b judge (evals/finetune/homograph_audit.py) were run and rejected as unreliable for this task: the first pass (naive prompt) over-triggered heavily, flagging genuine English-loanword synonym pairs as collisions (e.g. mobile->phone, test->exam, fridge->refrigerator, cycle->bicycle -- these are NOT collisions, same meaning, just a borrowed English word). A recalibrated few-shot prompt improved accuracy but hand-validation against 18 known-labeled cases still showed only 14/18 (78%) correct, including a false negative on a genuine collision (band/closed) -- unacceptable given the user's zero-tolerance framing. The final list below is a direct manual linguistic review of all 119 candidates (every crosslingual/LLM-augmented training pair whose Hindi-side token is also present in the game's curated English vocabulary, vocab.load_en_vocab()), superseding both automated runs.

collisions.door: English 'door' = entrance/hinged panel, vs Hindi 'door' = far. User-flagged example.
collisions.din: English 'din' = loud noise, vs Hindi 'din' = day.
collisions.band: English 'band' = musical group / strip of material, vs Hindi 'band' = closed.
collisions.pair: English 'pair' = two of a kind, vs Hindi 'pair' (पैर) = foot.
collisions.pet: English 'pet' = domesticated animal, vs Hindi 'pet' (पेट) = stomach.
collisions.chain: English 'chain' = linked rings / restrain, vs Hindi 'chain' (as in 'chain se') = peace.
collisions.beta: English 'beta' = Greek letter / pre-release software version, vs Hindi 'beta' = son.
collisions.pita: English 'pita' = flatbread (pita bread), vs Hindi 'pita' = father.
collisions.teen: English 'teen' = teenager, vs Hindi 'teen' = the number three.
collisions.agar: English 'agar' = gelatinous seaweed substance (agar plate/agar-agar), vs Hindi 'agar' = if.
collisions.koi: English 'koi' = ornamental fish (koi pond), vs Hindi 'koi' = someone.
collisions.mama: English colloquial 'mama' = mother, vs Hindi 'mama' = maternal uncle (gender-flipped collision).
collisions.nana: English colloquial 'nana' = grandmother, vs Hindi 'nana' = maternal grandfather (gender-flipped collision).

cleared_as_loanwords_or_synonyms.note: these ARE English words but their English meaning IS consistent with the Hinglish pairing -- borrowed/synonym pairs, not collisions.

fuzzy_negative_pairs_corrected.guru->music: removed -- guru is commonly a music/arts teacher in Indian classical tradition (sangeet guru), too related to serve as an 'unrelated' negative.
fuzzy_negative_pairs_corrected.jar->can: removed -- jar and can are near-synonym containers, not semantically unrelated.
